## SEVERE Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) Treated in Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
## Criteria for Defining SEVERE Community-acquired Pneumonia
Validated definition includes either one major or three or more minor criteria
MAJOR CRITERIA:
Septic shock with need for vasopressors
Respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
MINOR CRITERIA:
Respiratory rate greater than or equal to 30 breaths/minute
PaO2/FiO2 ratio less than or equal to 250
Multilobar infiltrates
Confusion/disorientation
Uremia (blood urea nitrogen level greater than 20 mg/dl)
Leukopenia* (WBC less than 4,000 cells/microliter)
*Due to infection alone (i.e., not chemotherapy induced)
Thrombocytopenia (platelet count less than 100,000 microliters)
Hypothermia (core temperature less than 36 degrees C)
Hypotension requiring aggressive fluid resuscitation
## Recommendation for duration of antibiotic therapy for CAP:
Patients with CAP should be treated for a minimum of 5 days, should be
afebrile for 48-72 hours, and should have no more than 1 CAP-
associated sign of clinical instability before discontinuation
of therapy.
## Criteria for clinical stability:
Temperature less than/equal to 100 degrees F
Heart rate less than/equal to 100 beats/minute
Respiratory rate less than/equal to 24 breaths/minute
Systolic blood pressure greater than/equal to 90 mm Hg
Arterial oxygen saturation greater than/equal to 90% --OR--
PO2 greater than/equal to 60 mm Hg on room air
Ability to maintain oral intake
Normal mental status

## Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for MRSA -OR-
## Prior Respiratory Isolation of MRSA within last 12 months:
ADD MRSA COVERAGE. Obtain nasal PCR and cultures to allow deescalation or
confirmation of need for continued therapy. SEE MRSA Section below
## Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for P. aeruginosa-OR
## Prior Respiratory Isolation of P. aeruginosa in the last 12 months:
COVER for P. aeruginosa. Obtain cultures to allow deescalation or
confirmation of need for continued therapy. SEE P. aeruginosa section below
## Preferred Standard Regimen: (no MRSA or P. aeruginosa coverage)
## Inpatient

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h($) [M] <AND> azithromycin 500 mg IV once
on day 1, then 250 mg IV Q24H for 4 days ($) [M]
## Alternative Standard Regimen:
Fluoroquinolones FDA Serious Adverse Reactions

< OR >
